content: 1. Evaluate the potential for environmental contamination and the spread of infection at destinations where inbound flights or ships from Ebola Virus Disease (EVD)-affected areas are arriving. 2. Assess whether special measures are required upon arrival at points of entry to mitigate risks. 3. Determine if the conveyance (aircraft or ship) requires any specific supplies to address public health concerns. 4. Consider whether the situation necessitates the involvement of health authorities or experts, such as clinicians, epidemiologists, environmental specialists, or experts in chemical or radiological event response. 5. Verify if the conveyance originates from an area where the World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended specific measures. 6. Confirm whether clinical specimens or environmental samples have been collected, or if health authorities need to collect them. 7. Identify the scheduled departure time of the conveyance. 8. Assess the number of connections to international or domestic points of entry to evaluate potential risks. 9. For aircraft, ensure the availability of the Health Part of the Aircraft General Declaration and Passenger Locator Cards. 10. For ships, ensure the availability of the Maritime Declaration of Health, ship sanitation certificates, medical logbooks, and a list of medicines as per national regulations. 11. The health authority at the point of entry (PoE) should coordinate with PoE operators, conveyance operators, and other stakeholders to ensure adequate port health staff, personal protective equipment (PPE), and disinfectants are available. 12. Collaborate with aircraft operators to determine suitable disinfectants, as sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is not acceptable for use on board aircraft. 13. Raise awareness among relevant personnel, including cargo handlers, that visibly soiled packages with blood or body fluids should not be handled. 14. Arrange for interpreters if necessary to facilitate communication. 15. If a traveler or crew member exhibits symptoms of EVD or is identified as a close contact of an EVD case, the PoE health authority should consider activating the contingency plan, which should include public health components such as PPE, medicines, cleaning and disinfection protocols, and waste disposal measures. 16. Communicate with other authorities or experts to assess public health risks, determine necessary control measures, and evaluate their effectiveness. 17. Authorize the disembarkation of travelers without illness or suspected EVD and conduct medical follow-up with passengers as needed. 18. Minimize contact between ground staff and ill travelers or contaminated environments. 19. Inspect the conveyance for environmental contamination and arrange for the collection of clinical specimens or environmental samples as per national practices. 20. Supervise cleaning staff to ensure the application of public health measures, including decontamination and disinfection. 21. Report the event to the International Health Regulations (IHR) National Focal Point (NFP) for further assessment and notification to WHO, as per national plans and protocols. 22. Arrange interviews and health assessments for affected individuals. 23. Ensure the space for health assessments has access to toilet facilities, seating, water, and washing facilities. 24. Establish communication with competent authorities at the next known port to inform them if required control measures cannot be implemented at the current port. 25. Maintain ongoing communication with conveyance operators (airlines, ships, ground vehicles), airport and air traffic services, and maritime and port authorities. 26. After travel, assess whether symptoms are consistent with EVD, such as fever, weakness, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, or bleeding. 27. Review the travel history of the individual to determine if they had contact with anyone suspected of EVD infection or traveled in EVD-affected areas. 28. Advise ill individuals to seek medical assessment and care at a hospital. 29. If recent travel history indicates contact with suspected EVD cases or travel in EVD-affected areas, initiate contact tracing to identify close contacts, such as passengers or crew seated near the ill traveler. 30. PoE health authorities should arrange for the repatriation of cases and the transportation of specimens as needed. 31. Strengthen communication between national health surveillance systems and PoE health authorities.
